plot: With a flat tyre and the new one only arriving at sunset, Turbo must stay all day in Bolt's warm garage while it rains; he tries once to sneak out and flops, so Bolt gives him a sitting-still case — find where the drip in the garage comes from before the puddle reaches Bolt's case notebook; Turbo listens and watches, works out the drip gets faster with the rain, and finds a red race-track leaf in the puddle: the drainpipe is blocked by the leaves Grumpy dumped there yesterday; Grumpy clears it, Dot the tyre van brings the new tyre at sunset, and Bertha splashes in with a new problem — her giant pumpkin won't fit through her door.

script.title: Can Turbo Sit Still Until Sunset?
script.description: A flat tyre, a rainy day and one drip that nobody can find. Inspector Bolt #31

set.place: Bolt's warm garage on Gear Street with its big window, a rainy autumn day from morning until sunset

beats.say: Bump, flop! Bump, flop! Bolt! Help! My tyre is flat!
Easy, Turbo. Come inside. Out of the rain.
It was a rainy autumn morning in Wheelburg. Drip, drop, drip.
Yesterday, Turbo raced on sharp old stones. Now his tyre was flat.
I called Dot, the tyre van. New tyre at sunset.
Sunset?! That's a whole day! What do I do all day?
You stay here, in my garage. No rolling on that tyre.
If you drive on it, your wheel could get hurt, Turbo.
And Bolt, all yesterday's leaves? I put them by your garage.
Up the side. By the drainpipe. Out of the way.
Thank you, Grumpy. Very tidy.
Grumpy and Pip drove off. Turbo was alone with Bolt.
One minute. I sat still for one whole minute.
That was eleven seconds, Turbo.
Okay. I'll count raindrops. One, two, three... boring!
Waiting is hard for everyone, Turbo. Even for detectives.
I can't do it! My wheels feel all wiggly!
Turbo tried to roll quietly to the door. Very, very slowly.
Flop! Flop! Floppity flop!
Turbo. Back you come. Gently.
Sorry. I'm just no good at waiting.
Drip. Drip. Plop.
Hmm. Did you hear that, Turbo?
A drip! Inside the garage! Where is it coming from?
A little puddle was creeping across the floor. Toward Bolt's blue notebook.
My case notebook! Every case I ever solved is in there!
I'll find the drip! I'll zoom around and look everywhere!
No zooming. Here is your case, Detective Turbo.
Find the drip. But your wheels must not move. Not once.
Solve a case without moving? Is that even allowed?
It's the hardest kind. Use your ears and your eyes.
Okay. Detective Turbo is on the case. Wheels... frozen!
So Turbo sat very still. And he listened.
Drip... drip... drip. It's not coming from the door.
And not from your hat hook, Bolt. Your hat is dry.
Good. What else do you notice?
The puddle starts under the big window. Not in the middle.
Outside, the rain got harder. Whoosh. Whoosh.
Listen! Now it goes drip-drip-drip-drip! Faster!
When the rain is fast, the drip is fast!
Excellent, Detective. The drip follows the rain.
But the puddle kept creeping. Closer and closer to the notebook.
Only a little bit more, and my notebook gets soaked!
Keep thinking, Turbo. I trust your eyes.
Don't move, don't move, don't move. Think, Turbo!
Something red was floating in the puddle. Round and round.
A leaf! A red leaf! Inside the garage!
Leaves don't grow in garages. So how did it get in?
It came with the water. Under the big window.
Wait. What did Grumpy say this morning?
By the drainpipe! The leaves are in the drainpipe!
So the rain can't go down the pipe.
So it spills over and comes in at the window! Case closed!
Detective Turbo solved it. And his wheels never moved.
Bolt called Grumpy. He came back through the rain.
My leaves did that? Sorry, Bolt.
It's okay, Grumpy! Your leaves gave me my first case!
Grumpy reached up with his hook. Scrape, scrape. Pull!
Whoosh! A big wet ball of leaves fell out of the pipe.
Gurgle, gurgle. Now the rain goes down. Where it belongs.
The drip stopped. My notebook is dry. Every page.
I sat still, Bolt. Did you see? Almost the whole day!
When your wheels must stop, your brain can still race.
At sunset, the rain stopped. And a green van rolled in.
Hello, hello! Dot's Tyres! One shiny new tyre for Turbo!
My tyre! My beautiful round tyre! I missed you!
You didn't even meet it yet, sweetie.
Pop, click, done. Turbo had four good wheels again.
Now go easy on those old white stones, okay?
I promise! Around them, not over them!
Zoom time! Wait. Can I tell you about my case first?
A car who wants to talk before zooming? That's new!
Then Pip zoomed in, splashing through the puddles.
Turbo! You've got a new tyre! Hooray!
Pip! I solved a case! Sitting still! Ask Bolt!
You? Sitting still? Is that true, Bolt?
Every word of it.
And right behind her came Big Bertha. Very upset.
Bolt! It's my pumpkin! My giant pumpkin for the Harvest Fair!
It grew SO big, it won't fit out of my depot door!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
